assignments.summary: A 1993 Usenet thread discusses a poll of Ivy League students identifying as atheists, comparing it to general population beliefs about reincarnation and the rise of smoking and supernatural beliefs. Participants debate reasons for the discrepancy, including intelligence, age, and the social environment of college campuses, with international perspectives shared from an Asian context.

This Reuters news feature from 1993 documents Neret Mujanovic, a pathologist from Tuzla who volunteered as a surgeon in the besieged Muslim town of Srebrenica during Bosnia's year-long siege. After trekking through mountains under guerrilla protection, he performed over 1,300 major surgeries—including 150 amputations and 350 deliveries—largely without anesthetic or proper facilities, treating roughly 4,000 patients while enduring daily shelling, severe supply shortages, and the deaths of civilians, particularly children. His account describes the collapse of medical infrastructure, the arrival of MSF supplies in December 1993 as a turning point, and the subsequent U.S. air-drop of food that prevented mass starvation through mid-1994. The article serves as a firsthand testament to the medical and humanitarian crisis in Srebrenica.

A 1993 Usenet post from the dct.ac.uk domain featuring a heated political debate between John Bell and Dan Sorenson (DoD #1066) discussing monarchy, federal agents, and gun control rhetoric. The exchange includes provocative statements about monarchy supporters, federal violence at Waco/CNN reports, and trans-Atlantic class differences in political discourse. Posted to what appears to be an academic or research network discussion group.

A brief internal-style note referencing a CNN report questioning the impartiality of the team that investigated the Waco fire, alleging the team leader's spouse is a BATF agent. The author dismisses the government's continuation of the investigation as propaganda and includes a standard secure-line disclaimer with a contact entry for Daniel R. Oldham.

A 1993 email exchange between James Kiefer and Tony Zamora regarding the interpretation of 2 Peter 1:20, specifically debating whether scriptural prophecy is merely the private opinion of the writer or immune to private reader interpretation. The discussion uses historical examples to illustrate the tension between objective fact and subjective assent.

A user posts a question on an automotive forum about why a 4WD Vauxhall/Opel vehicle disengages rear-wheel drive when the brakes are applied, referencing the manufacturer's claim that the car is more stable in front-wheel-drive mode during braking, and asking for an explanation of the underlying mechanism.

An email from Anthony at the University of Adelaide's Medicine department reporting that a LaserWriter Select 310 printer connected to an LC III running System 7.1 fails to detect Adobe Type 1 or TrueType fonts despite correct installation. The sender shares the installed driver versions and seeks community insight, expressing frustration that an Apple product does not work out of the box.

A Usenet forum post from the late 1990s where a rider describes fixing a Mikuni HS40 carburetor by tightening loose internal screws, offering a roadside repair tip to fellow motorcyclists. The thread includes signature blocks with amateur radio call signs and motorcycle club affiliations.

A 1993 Usenet post shares an abstract investigating whether gamma-ray bursts could originate from the Oort cloud of comets, analyzing BATSE data and cometary orbit catalogs to test for statistical correlations, concluding that while a connection is unlikely, it cannot be ruled out with current data.

A 1996 email thread from Cliff at the University of South Dakota sharing a uuencoded 960x600 256-color bitmap of a marbled gazebo, responding to requests for cool images. The sender complains that the large file caused excessive modem connect time and cost an extra $3.00, advising alternative distribution methods like FTP sites or dedicated newsgroups instead of discussion groups. The email includes technical details about the image's suitability for 1024x768 wallpaper.

A 1993 email exchange between Brad Yearwood and Perry Metzger discussing the technical and policy mechanics of the Clipper Chip proposal, specifically focusing on how serial numbers embedded in cipher streams could aid law enforcement identification under wiretap orders.

A Usenet post from the early 1990s describing a quirk where switching between full-screen DOS and Windows caused desktop fonts to scramble, with users sharing workarounds involving WIN.INI configuration and full-screen DOS session exits.

A 1990s Usenet post discussing Toyota MR2 engine specifications, comparing first and second generation models, and debating patent ownership of balancing shaft technology among Japanese manufacturers.

A 1993 Usenet post from jerry@doodles.informix.com troubleshooting the 'space: out of memory' error in the Startrek version of Afterdark, a screen saver, while John A. Grant from the Geological Survey of Canada provides the correct tagline. The message reflects early 1990s retro-computing culture and technical support via email.

A researcher from the University of Notre Dame's Radiation Laboratory inquired about bibliography/referencing software capable of database management and journal-specific formatting for scientific publications. The email seeks recommendations for a single tool to organize literature used in refereeing papers.

A 1993 Usenet/email theological discussion about the location of paradise before Christ's resurrection, referencing Luke 23:43, Luke 16:19-31, and Ephesians 4:8 to argue that 'Abraham's Bosom' (infernal paradise) was a section of hades reserved for believers who awaited resurrection. The author engages with a critic named Rick Anderson, defending scriptural interpretation and addressing objections about differing views on biblical meaning.

An email thread from the late 1980s/early 1990s discussing the necessity of loading EMM386 with the 'noems' option to access upper memory between 640KB and 1MB for DOS kernel and device drivers. The author argues it is unnecessary for their specific use case of running ProcommPlus, while a respondent recommends removing it to avoid potential slowdowns of Windows.

A 1993 Usenet email thread from the Ingres Corporation domain featuring heated personal insults directed at Michael Friedman and Phil Ronzone, with the author playfully questioning whether they still hold controversial technical opinions about the M-16 firearm and the application of 14th Amendment clauses to the federal government. The message exemplifies early internet flame-war culture and netiquette violations.

A Usenet-style forum post from the early 1990s discussing the COSE (Consortium/Common Open Software Environment) standard and the Motif GUI toolkit. The author poses several unresolved technical questions about whether Motif will become the universal look and feel for COSE-compliant applications, the implications for API toolkit compliance, and how ToolTalk integration fits into the standard. The post invites discussion and knowledge-sharing among readers.

A 1990s-era email inquiry asking whether the cryptographic transport protocol RIPEM has been ported to the Amiga personal computer platform, sent by Ken Guyton of Emory University's Information Technology Division. The message reflects early internet-era curiosity about software compatibility across emerging hardware.

A 1990s Usenet post proposing the development of a general-purpose hardware device for interactive internet talk radio, suggesting the Sun workstation as a starting point to build momentum among homebrewers. The author offers to start a provisional mailing list and invites interested parties to collaborate on protocol experimentation.

This file is a 1990s-era technical announcement and distribution list for PGP (Pretty Good Privacy) encryption software, listing executable formats and source code availability across multiple platforms (MS-DOS, Mac, UNIX, Amiga, OS/2, etc.) and providing FTP and BBS access points for retrieval. It serves as a public service announcement from a BBS SysOp, noting platform availability and directing users to specific archive sites.

A Usenet post from 1995 requesting references to a 1993 Associated Press article describing BATF agents throwing grenades during the initial raid on the Davidian compound. The post includes a brief recollection from a University of Tennessee continuing education contact and a 'Weird Al' quote, reflecting early internet-era discussion of the Waco stand-off.

A 1990s Usenet/email thread from Boston University and University of Arizona affiliates debating Islamic scripture, the literary quality of the Qur'an, and historical authenticity, with participants questioning authorship and textual preservation while referencing translation issues and marital regulations.

A 1980s Usenet post by Josh Schwimmer discusses Burzynski's antineoplaston research, summarizing NCI test results against various cancer types and noting the chemical relationships between A-10, PAG, and thalidomide. The post critiques Burzynski's claims about A-10's antineoplastic activity and highlights unresolved questions about A-1 through A-5 being distinct substances.

A brief recollection of Brooks Robinson's final career home run, which occurred on April 19, 1977, at Memorial Stadium, where he hit a walk-off three-run blast in the bottom of the 10th inning to secure a 6-5 victory for the Baltimore Orioles. The account notes Larry Harlow was due to bat next, but Robinson pinch-hit the decisive pitch from Dave LaRoche.

A 1993 Usenet post from a NEC researcher recommending Goo Gone for cleaning chain grime and bug splatter, comparing its effectiveness to Simple Green and noting the author's continued use of PJ-1 and Goo products after a UPS loss. The post includes personal biking references and a humorous suggestion to brand Goo Gone as a "DoD Wonder Spooge (tm)" product.

A 1993 Usenet post from Charles Parr enthusiastically reviewing bicycle maintenance products, specifically Chain Wax and a clear RF-200 face shield, while complaining about a delayed order from Competition Accessories. Dean Cookson adds a signature block referencing his MITRE affiliation and two motorcycles. The post serves as a informal product endorsement and a complaint about mail-order fulfillment times in the early 1990s.

A user troubleshoots a monochrome display issue when running Xsun on Sun-3 4/110 workstations with a cgtwo0 color framebuffer, noting that static compilation and the Xnews dynamically linked alternative produce different results, and references specific hardware and software versions (gcc 2.3.3, SunOS 4.1.3) and kernel device nodes.

A seller offers 13 used Kimble Modern Liebig condensers (500mm jacket length) from original packaging, priced at $15 each with volume discounts up to 30% for bulk purchases. The listing includes details on insurance, shipping estimates, and quality control notes, and references comparable Central Scientific series equipment.

The text presents a theological argument comparing Protestant and Catholic views on infant baptism, centering on the concepts of original sin, sanctifying grace, and the spiritual maturity required for faith. It uses scriptural references from Romans and Ezekiel to support the claim that babies cannot have faith and therefore, from a Protestant perspective, cannot be baptized, while Catholics baptize infants to impart grace originally lost through Adam's sin.

An email exchange between astein@nysernet.org and an individual at virginia.edu discusses university policies on free speech versus hate speech, comparing Virginia.edu's open approach to perceived restrictions at Israel.nysernet.org, with references to Thomas Jefferson and the Bill of Rights.

A 1993 Usenet post by Lynn R Grant discussing the Clipper Chip proposal and its implications for privacy, specifically debating whether the FBI could access encrypted past and future traffic with court orders. The post includes a proposed modification regarding phone replacement if charges are dropped, and reflects broader concerns about government surveillance and NIST/NSA authority.

A 1993 email thread between Sherri Nichols and others discussing the Hart Trophy, debating whether the award should go to the most valuable player to his team versus the best player in the league, reflecting on how the award's meaning has changed with professionalism in hockey.

A 1993 Usenet discussion about whether "everyone" includes infants and young children, sparked by a theological debate. Participants Brian Ceccarelli and Ken Arromdee argue that even very young children demonstrate agency and resistance (e.g., sticking fingers in sockets, fighting diaper changes), suggesting personhood-like behavior from birth. An Apple employee (Sandvik) adds a brief technical note about infant cognitive development in the first six months.

An internal email exchange between Gary Sager and Charles Herbig discussing the proper procedure for powering off employee monitors at the end of the workday, noting a design concern regarding monitors with rear-mounted power switches that may not tolerate frequent power cycling. The conversation includes a philosophical reflection on why controls are often placed in hard-to-reach locations.

An online forum exchange between Kenneth Engel and Chris Mussack discussing the theological implications of Jesus' suffering versus eternal hell, focusing on whether Christ's brief suffering adequately atones for human sin and how this relates to the concept of eternal punishment.

A personal email excerpt from Jake Livni reflecting on casualty figures in Lebanon and the Iran-Iraq conflict, noting regional animosity toward Zionists and a brief, speculative question about the correlation between anti-Israel sentiment and internal violence. The text includes a follow-up question about Iranian identity relative to Arab classification.

An email thread between Steve Novak and a UChicago mailing list debating the purpose and appropriateness of a moment of silence in public schools, with arguments centering on religious neutrality, taxpayer funding, and student autonomy. The discussion critiques both mandatory participation and blind opposition to religion, framing the issue as a defense against Christianity becoming the official U.S. religion.

The author requests documented evidence against the Branch Davidians, rejecting hearsay and media reports, prompted by a "cult-expert" appearance on Larry King Live who claimed his evidence triggered the original raid. The writer references classic anti-cult scholarship by Shupe and Bromley, expressing concern that government actions may have been based on faulty advice from self-proclaimed experts, drawing parallels to the Waco tragedy.

A brief text snippet requesting email subscription, containing an email address associated with the domain porto.inescn.pt. The document appears to be a standalone user request or form fragment for joining a mailing list.

A 1993 Boston Globe article reports on a Walpole man's guilty plea for kidnapping, rape, and beating a mother of two, as well as an attempted jail escape. The piece notes the defendant's prior 15-year sentence for a rape committed at age 16 and the timing of the current crime relative to his release. The article includes a brief reader comment from J. Case Kim discussing the adequacy of the sentence.

A 1993 email exchange between Peter (pww@rice.edu) and Kent, discussing the relationship between Jesus, logic, and faith. The conversation critiques the use of logic to interpret biblical parables and includes a signature referencing private activities on the Newton network at Apple.

A 1993 Usenet discussion thread where participants reference a Budweiser advertisement flying through the sky, tracing the idea back to Jules Verne and debating its origins. The exchange includes Jeff Cook and Phil Fraering, hosted on the cs.lbl.gov domain.

A 1990s usenet post by Matt Coohill on wavefront.wti.com complaining about ESPN's inconsistent NHL playoff broadcast schedule, specifically the switching between advertised Pittsburgh/NJ and Boston/Buffalo games, with the author expressing frustration over the perceived poor scheduling decisions and betting on exciting matchups.

A private party listing for a 1990 Pontiac Grand Prix SE coupe with extensive power options and low mileage, sold by an individual in the Boston area due to an upcoming baby. The seller is open to trade offers for 4-door American sedans.

A user posts to a 1994 computing forum describing intermittent Windows 3.1 lockups on a new Dell 486DX2/66 with 8MB RAM after a motherboard replacement. The community troubleshoots the issue as a high memory conflict between video RAM and system memory, suggesting EMMEXCLUDE statements in SYSTEM.INI and CONFIG.SYS to resolve the instability.

A Usenet flame war between Alexander P. Zijdenbos and Thomas Kettenring about Kirlian photography and paranormal beliefs, where Zijdenbos argues for keeping an open mind while Kettenring accuses skeptics of closed-mindedness and adds a remark about extraterrestrials not knowing Earth has native inhabitants.

A user inquiring about compatibility between a vintage VXC Moniterm 19-inch black-and-white monitor (marked Viking 2/90 with a DB9 connector) and Macintosh computers, seeking advice on required hardware cards. The post references prior use on an Atari ST and asks for technical guidance on adapter cards.

A developer reports a bug in Motif 1.2 on HPUX 9.01 where Japanese text entered into an XmTextField is truncated at display time, while the same text works correctly in English locales. The issue is linked to LC_ALL environment variable settings and does not occur with XmText widgets. The author provides a small test program to illustrate the problem and suspects improper memory allocation for Kanji characters by X or Motif.

A 1993 Usenet post from the ri.cadre.com newsgroup in which a user asks whether it is legal to export DES encryption code to Canada, receiving a response that such transmission generally requires an export license and noting the distinction between licensed and unlicensed transfers.

A 1990s-era email from Michael Adams to a mailing list discussing an economical approach to interplanetary exploration. The writer proposes designing a mother ship capable of carrying multiple piggy‑back probes to different planets, leveraging a solar sail for propulsion and drawing a parallel to Cold War MIRV missile principles. The concept aims to reduce launch costs by sending several probes on a single mission, with the Mars mission potentially serving as a relay point for other probes.

A 1993 Usenet post from Bob Wilson warns consumers about Midwest Micro, an Ohio-based company selling defective and used modems as new, detailing how their products damaged his hardware and how the company refused to take responsibility. Another user shares a similar experience with a used trackball sold as new at a local Micro Center, advising the poster to demand a PUS PULL TAG replacement.

A satirical opinion piece proposing that adding cheerleaders and intentional bench-clearing brawls would increase baseball's popularity, contrasting the sport's "laid-back" reputation with the sex-and-violence formula supposedly driving other major American sports. The author critiques current baseball culture while suggesting exaggerated reforms.

A 1990s Usenet forum post recapping a hockey trivia query about NHL players who appeared on national talk shows. It details Tod Hartje's unique career path, including playing in the Soviet Union and appearing on David Letterman to discuss his experiences chronicled in his book 'Behind the Red Line.'

A personal reflection on the ethics and practicality of space advertising, responding to Carl Sagan's criticism. The author argues that while space advertising is a valid experiment, companies must weigh potential revenue against brand damage from public backlash, noting that social ills like child poverty are truly abominable compared to advertising in poor taste.

A user named Bob Kehoe shares his experience with a V6 engine's fuel economy, noting poor mileage in city driving (<15 mpg) and average highway performance (~21 mpg). Another user counters with their Nissan Quest achieving 20 mpg city and 21 mpg highway, praising the V6 and automatic transmission for smooth operation. The post originates from an ncube.com forum and includes a signature block from Johnny P. Stephens of Arizona State University.

A faculty member named Mike Brooks is seeking online access to proposed 'jobs' or 'stimulus' legislation and requests that interested parties contact him directly. He notes his email header address is incorrect and provides a corrected address ending in ifas.ufl.edu.

A user posting to the sci.electronics newsgroup in 1993 requests assistance locating a copy of the PCMCIA hardware standard, specifically reaching out to contacts associated with ProControl in Kemptville, ON. The message also references OLX 2.1, an early bulletin-board / early internet forum software platform.

A 1993 Usenet email thread discussing Kirlian photography, a technique that captures corona discharges using high voltage rather than photographing auras. Participants correct spelling and clarify the scientific basis of the method, referencing its applicability to both animate and inanimate objects.

Claude Bowie shared a news report about research suggesting vitamin A may improve hearing by regenerating damaged hairlike nerves. The message includes his FedEx contact information and was likely distributed internally or to a small group. No school or workplace context is present.

An email thread discussing the feasibility of constructing an LED array for a window display, where each LED is approximately half an inch square, must be highly transparent to remain invisible, and cost is a primary constraint. The sender seeks suggestions on materials and construction methods while keeping the design details vague.

A reflective personal email from the late 1960s or early 1970s critiquing the perceived complacency of the era and expressing disappointment with the youth of the time. The author references political unrest, protests, and the contrast between revolutionary fervor and what they view as negligent outcomes.

An engineering email thread from the early 1990s discussing methods for constructing non-standard resistor values for active filter design, exploring options such as using parallel resistor combinations, higher-tolerance components, and trimmers. The correspondence originates from the Inquiring Mind BBS and includes technical constraints around 1% tolerance devices.

A Usenet newsgroup post from the 1990s where John E. King shares a Library of Congress catalog listing of books by Francis Hitching, sparking a discussion about anthropological parallels and the tactics of critics who discredit sources. The post includes a philosophical quote from Johannes Scotus Eriugena about the conflict between reason and authority.

A 1993 Usenet forum post in which a user named Robbie Po laments the absence of Boston Bruins fans online during the playoffs, compares the Bruins' performance to the New York Rangers' collapse, and discusses specific players like Mogilny and the matchup against the Pittsburgh Penguins. The post reflects regional hockey rivalries and playoff anticipation.

George Paap shares his personal skepticism about deep abdominal massage, a fringe massage technique that claims to loosen undigested food and toxins from the intestines. He dismisses the practice as quack science, comparing it to chiropracty, and uses a New York City sewer pipe analogy to argue the idea is physiologically implausible.

A Usenet newsgroup post from May 1993 discussing theological interpretations of the Christian Trinity, comparing modalistic views (Monarchianism, Economic Trinitarianism) against other descriptions, with the author seeking an orthodox yet believable explanation of how God can be both three and one.

A Usenet newsgroup post from Bill Conner on okcforum.osrhe.edu debating the logical consistency of a perfect, all-knowing creator god, referencing arguments about omniscience and contradictory definitions, and citing Desmond Morris's book Manwatching as an explanation for religious belief.

A Usenet newsgroup post from the early 1990s seeking sources for TrueType font files containing Japanese hiragana and katakana syllabaries, reflecting early Windows platform demand for Japanese language support before widespread Unicode adoption.
A brief classified advertisement offering a 24-bit color 600 DPI flatbed scanner capable of scanning GIF, TIFF, PCX, and BMP formats. The seller provides an AOL email contact for interested buyers.

A 1993 Usenet post in the talk.politics.groups newsgroup presents statistical arguments about home gun ownership, citing a 43-to-1 ratio of gun-related deaths to intruder killings, and references an earlier study suggesting guns are 33 times more likely to be used in defense than to cause death. The author invites further research into ratios for non-gun-owning households.

An email thread from 1999 discussing the temperature of the night sky as seen from space, citing Allen's Astrophysical Quantities (3K) and Eddington's earlier work (1926). The discussion references the radiation of starlight as the source and includes a note from Tom Van Flandern of Meta Research, an organization founded to support non-mainstream astronomical ideas.

A 1990s Usenet newsgroup post discussing whether IBM and Microsoft subsidized third-party application development for their respective operating systems, OS/2 and Windows NT. The author references a anecdote about a recipient at RPI receiving a machine for NT development.

A 1990s email from Bill Ray at Louisiana Tech University explores philosophical questions about burden of proof, using hypothetical scenarios with space aliens, Elvis, Bigfoot, and blue unicorns to examine how people evaluate extraordinary claims and personal testimony.

A 1993 email from Dick Detweiler proposing the creation of a mailing list for fans of the 1993 championship team, seeking technical guidance on setup and management. The message was sent from an HP corporate email address and reflects early internet community-building efforts around sports fandom.

A 1993 Usenet newsgroup post discussing potential NHL realignment scenarios, specifically debating where the Hamilton Oilers would be placed if they relocated, with speculation about Winnipeg or Dallas moving to the Pacific division. The post includes a signature from Tom Moffat in Victoria, BC.

This document is a curated collection of quotations attributed to Zionist leaders and Israeli officials, spanning from the late 19th century to 1983. Sourced from scholarly works and newspapers, the excerpts address themes of land acquisition, population transfer, military strategy, and ideological statements regarding the Palestinian presence and the establishment of the Jewish state. The collection was compiled by Elias Davidsson and shared via the Center for Policy Research, inviting verification of source authenticity. It serves as a primary-source reference for scholars examining the historical narrative of the Palestine question and the rhetoric surrounding Zionist colonization and state-building.

A 1993 Usenet post on the rec.motorcycles newsgroup where Erik Asphaug shares ownership experience with a BMW R80GS, offering practical advice on fairing modifications, electrical system considerations, cold-start techniques, and ethanol-compatible carburetor upgrades while engaging with community questions about long-distance riding and peripheral lighting.

Tony is planning a summer trip to Toronto and wants to attend a Toronto Blue Jays baseball game, seeking advice on obtaining tickets, preferably good seats, and asking for broker information or direct team channels. He mentions he will bring oxygen if needed and is flexible on game choices but prefers Texas matchups.

A 1990s Usenet post by Kin Cho on the polaris.isi.com forum requests a PostScript-to-plain-text converter that retains page counts. David Wagner (dawagner@princeton.edu) responds with a description of ghostscript's gs_2asc.ps filter and shares a custom C program called "massager" that extracts ASCII strings from PostScript output, noting the tool sometimes breaks up words or sentences.

A 1993 Usenet post from a first-time user on the Montana State University network expressing concern about the Waco incident and sharing a 'Weird Al' Yankovic lyric, while noting the absence of a FAQ for the TPG (likely a technical or user group). The post originates from the University of Tennessee Division of Continuing Education and reflects early internet discourse on political actions and community norms.

A 1970s Usenet discussion thread examining the history and regulation of subliminal perception in media, referencing FCC rules 73.4250, the 1950s popcorn-sales panic, and real-world cases like a failed single-frame commercial insertion. The author notes that while one-frame edits are technically visible on VCRs, brand placement via convenient product visibility remains a persistent practice requiring promotional consideration disclosures.

An early 1992 Usenet/email exchange in which Alyn Kelley shares a lighthearted observation about police officers giving friendly waves versus the more common negative encounters, contrasting their experience with a friend's history of being pulled over and shouted at, and concluding with a philosophical note about trading serious interactions for simple goodwill.

A 1990s-era classified advertisement from Donald Lyles selling a SIM card from a Palm Pilot 100 (PB100) for $60, including postage. The seller provides an email address for internet users and a phone number (301/468-0241) for those without internet access.

A 1990s-style email thread posted to a mailing list where Peter Nesbitt asks how to obtain copies of anti-gun legislation, with the House Document Room providing the phone number (202-225-3456) and document reference requirements, while the Senate directs requests by mail only. The message reflects early internet culture of gathering gun-rights education and legislative information.

A Usenet-style email thread from the early internet era discussing motorcycle steering mechanics, specifically the concept of countersteering and no-hands riding technique, featuring technical explanation and informal biker anecdotes.

A 1993 Usenet newsgroup thread discussing the technique of 'neutral slamming' or 'rocking' automatic transmissions, specifically GM's TH400 and TH350 models, with users sharing experiences about durability, peeling out, and modifications. The conversation includes technical details about shifting patterns, engine RPMs, and aftermarket modifications.

A Usenet newsgroup post from the 1990s discussing plans to re-boost the Hubble Space Telescope's orbit from 180 miles to 220 miles. The post originates from the digex.net domain and reflects early internet discussions about space telescope maintenance.

A Usenet discussion from the 1990s in which participants debate statistics regarding the percentage of homosexual individuals, referencing the Janus Report and arguing about methodology, anonymity, and reported numbers related to child molestation claims.

A 1993 Usenet discussion critiques the credibility of Moss, the Director of Communications for People Against Cancer, questioning the validity and safety of alternative cancer treatments promoted by the organization. The poster argues that the NIH's findings against such therapies are biased and that patient testimonials should hold more weight than regulatory agencies. The exchange reflects broader skepticism toward mainstream medical research and the influence of vested interests in alternative medicine debates.

A 1993 Usenet email thread from Eric Rescorla discussing the appropriateness and purpose of a 'moment of silence' in a high school setting, specifically in response to a classmate's death and the potential for the practice to be used as a vehicle for school prayer. The discussion explores the distinction between silent reflection and overt religious endorsement, with participants debating whether the tradition can coexist with attempts to reintroduce organized prayer.

A student shares her experience of a delayed kidney stone diagnosis and subsequent wait for surgery, expressing frustration over excessive x-rays, lack of pain medication, and a three-month queue. She seeks clarification on the imaging process and considers obtaining a second opinion.

A newsgroup post from the late 1980s reviewing the film "Eat the Peach," which uses a motorcycle-built "wall of death" as a narrative device to explore themes of boredom and political tension in rural Ireland, touching on IRA involvement. The post includes a signature block listing the author's motorcycles and affiliations with AHRMA and AMA.

A 1990s Usenet post in which a user documents the visual differences in window chrome (tile and scroll bars) after upgrading from a Trident TVGA9000 to an ATI Graphics Ultra card, seeking .ini-level configuration fixes; a responder advises selecting the small fonts driver over the large fonts driver.

A brief, provocative fragment that challenges the nature of shared experience and consensual reality, offering no context or resolution. The text functions as a standalone philosophical provocation rather than a document with a specific purpose or audience.

A 1993 Usenet newsgroup post from David Howarth at Southwestern Bell Technology Resources discussing a hockey game, specifically debating the whereabouts of Roenick relative to Bassen and commenting on Belfour's performance. The post reflects typical early internet sports forum culture with signature formatting and regional references.

A 1990s Usenet discussion thread where a user questions the etiquette of copying entire article histories with only a name appended at the end, debating whether this practice signifies agreement or is simply redundant. The post references energy conservation regarding personal computers and includes a signature from Susanmarie Harrington at the University of Michigan.

A Usenet/forum thread excerpt from the early 1990s discussing the technical feasibility of running high-power ham radio transmitters (up to 1500 watts) from a vehicle, focusing on alternator capacity, power conversion (PeP vs real watts), and antenna effects. Participants debate power requirements, share anecdotes about modified car rigs, and reference technical details like Klystron output and antenna gain.

A brief text post by Markus listing and questioning country-code top-level domain extensions, specifically noting Switzerland (ch), Sweden (se), Finland (fi), the UK (uk), and debating whether US domains are limited to .com and .edu or also include other variants. The file includes a signature and an unrelated signature block featuring car imagery.

A Usenet newsgroup discussion from the early 1990s debating the legitimacy of physical play in playoff hockey, specifically focusing on a controversial two-handed slash by Felix Potvin on Dino Ciccarelli that crossed the line from legal contact into an attempt to injure. The author argues that while some physicality is expected in front of the net, Potvin's action was motivated by frustration and immaturity, contrasting it with the accepted styles of tougher goaltenders like Billy Smith and Ron Hextall.

A Usenet post from 1992 discussing the mechanism of acetaminophen (paracetamol) toxicity, focusing on the formation of the toxic metabolite NAPQI, glutathione depletion, and the resulting hepatic necrosis. The author corrects a peer's description of the metabolic pathway and references a key review article on the subject, concluding with a shared sentiment about the severity of acetaminophen overdose.

A user named J. Watson posted a request on a forum seeking an FTP site to access the Vatican Library's recently completed US tour collection, which includes rare books and manuscripts now available stateside.
